Counsel for Applicant :- Ashok Kumar Chaubey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ram Raksha Tiwari
Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.
Short counter affidavit on behalf of opposite party no. 2 is taken on record.
2. Heard counsel for the applicant, Sri Ram Raksha Tiwari, counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the entire proceedings of Case No.
680/IX/2020 (State vs. Haridesh Kumar @ Mitesh Kumar), arising out of the Case Crime No. 14 of 2017, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Banda.

sentences.text: Considering that the matter had emanated from a matrimonial dispute between the husband and the wife, vide order dated 19.09.2023 passed by this Court, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre of this Court for exploring the possibility of settlement between the parties.
5. As per the report of the Mediation Centre dated 05.02.2023, the parties voluntarily arrived at a compromise.

In view of the Interim Settlement Agreement dated 22.01.2023, the following settlement has been arrived at between the Parties hereto:-
a) That the parties have filed a petition u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court, Banda and the same is registered as Case No. 38 of 2023.
The parties stated that all the terms and conditions mentioned therein have been fulfilled.
They further reiterated and reaffirm the terms and conditions of the aforesaid settlement and the same shall be a part of the settlement also.
The certified copy of the aforesaid divorce petition is being annexed to this settlement-agreement for kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court.

b) That it has been agreed between the parties that the applicant-husband shall pay one time settlement amount of Rs. 20,40,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs Fouty Thousand Only) which includes permanent alimony and Stridhan of the wife by way of Demand Draft.

c) That on 22.01.2023, the applicant-husband has produced two demand drafts bearing nos. 278769 & 278770 both dated 18.01.2023 both drawn on Bank of Baroda for Rs. 5,00,000/- & Rs. 5,20,000/- (Total Rupees Ten Lakhs Twenty Thousand only) in favour of Arti Devi (wife) and the same has been handed over to the wife today i.e. 05.02.2023 and she has acknowledged the receipt of the same.

d) That it has been agreed between the parties that the remaining amount i.e. Rs.
10,20,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Twenty Thousand only) shall be paid by Shri Hridesh Kumar @ Mitesh Kumar (Applicant- Husband) to Smt. Kumkum @ Arti (O.P. No. 2-Wife) at the time of final judgment in Case No. 38 of 2023 pending in Family Court, Banda by way of demand draft.

e) That it has also been agreed between the parties that all civil and criminal cases filed by them against each other regarding present matrimonial dispute shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the Court/authority concerned.

Hridesh Kumar @ Mitesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150073650/
2 f)

entities.text: Hridesh Kumar @ Mitesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That the parties will not file any fresh case against each other in respect of this matrimonial dispute.
They have no claim against each other in future also.
g) That it has been agreed between the parties that they shall not violate the terms and conditions of this settlement otherwise the aggrieved party will be free to take legal recourse.

8. By signing this Agreement the Parties hereto state that the Application U/S 482 No. 4570 of 2022 and all disputes and differences in this regard have been amicably settled by the Parties hereto through the process of Conciliation/ Mediation."
6.
Counsel for the opposite party no. 2 submits that the opposite party no. 2 has no objection if the proceedings are quashed.

7. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing a prosecution to proceed any further.

8. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T. 2008(9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.

Considering that the matter had emanated from a matrimonial dispute between the husband and the wife, vide order dated 19.09.2023 passed by this Court, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre of this Court for exploring the possibility of settlement between the parties.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The relevant paragraphs of the settlement agreement are extracted below;
"6. The parties hereto confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and of their own free will arrived at this Settlement Agreement in the presence of the Mediators/Conciliators.
7.
In view of the Interim Settlement Agreement dated 22.01.2023, the following settlement has been arrived at between the Parties hereto:-
a) That the parties have filed a petition u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court, Banda and the same is registered as Case No. 38 of 2023.
The parties stated that all the terms and conditions mentioned therein have been fulfilled.
They further reiterated and reaffirm the terms and conditions of the aforesaid settlement and the same shall be a part of the settlement also.
b) That it has been agreed between the parties that the applicant-husband shall pay one time settlement amount of Rs. 20,40,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs Fouty Thousand Only) which includes permanent alimony and Stridhan of the wife by way of Demand Draft.
c) That on 22.01.2023, the applicant-husband has produced two demand drafts bearing nos. 278769 & 278770 both dated 18.01.2023 both drawn on Bank of Baroda for Rs. 5,00,000/- & Rs. 5,20,000/- (Total Rupees Ten Lakhs Twenty Thousand only) in favour of Arti Devi (wife) and the same has been handed over to the wife today i.e. 05.02.2023 and she has acknowledged the receipt of the same.
d) That it has been agreed between the parties that the remaining amount i.e. Rs.
10,20,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Twenty Thousand only) shall be paid by Shri Hridesh Kumar @ Mitesh Kumar (Applicant- Husband) to Smt. Kumkum @ Arti (O.P. No. 2-Wife) at the time of final judgment in Case No. 38 of 2023 pending in Family Court, Banda by way of demand draft.
e) That it has also been agreed between the parties that all civil and criminal cases filed by them against each other regarding present matrimonial dispute shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the Court/authority concerned.
That the parties will not file any fresh case against each other in respect of this matrimonial dispute.
They have no claim against each other in future also.
8. By signing this Agreement the Parties hereto state that the Application U/S 482 No. 4570 of 2022 and all disputes and differences in this regard have been amicably settled by the Parties hereto through the process of Conciliation/ Mediation."
6.
Counsel for the opposite party no. 2 submits that the opposite party no. 2 has no objection if the proceedings are quashed.
9. The present application is, accordingly, allowed.
